Read by run-form-gate.mjs step 11, which recomputes every entry FROM WHAT THE FILLED PDF PRINTS and compares it to the printed figure. No figure lives here except the ones the FORM ITSELF PRINTS as constants — the $1,000 on line (1), the $3,450 vehicle allowance on line (6b), and the .8 quick-sale multiplier that appears five times — and every one is quoted from the caption that prints it.
authored_from: The printed page text of adapters/pdf/forms/f433aoi.pdf, extracted from the content streams and read alongside the widget rectangles by adapters/pdf/align-block.mjs. Captions below are quoted verbatim. NOT from field names: ELEVEN leaf names on this form are known to be actively wrong about what their cell means — including the page-3 pair Total_Value_Vehicles_Attached[0] and Enter_Allowance[0], which are printed lines (6d) and (6e) respectively and so hold each other's job. One of the eleven — RetirementAcct2[0].CurrentMarketValue[0].Times_7[0] — is a feeder of entry (3a) QSV below, where the leaf says .7 and the page says .8.
_slice: PRINTED PAGES 1 THROUGH 8. Every printed total on the form is either checked here or declared not checkable with a reason.
_notes: THIS FILE EXISTS BECAUSE THE SCHEMA CAN NOW CARRY THE FORM. It was deliberately not authored during slice 2: the feeder schema then added and subtracted and had no factor and no constant, so (3a)'s X .8 and (1)'s minus $1,000 — the two cells on page 2 that most need checking — would have been the two it could not express. Nine clean passes printed beside two silently-absent checks is worse than a SKIP that says nothing was checked.

A FACTOR AND A CONSTANT, NOT AN EXPRESSION LANGUAGE. `factor` and `constant` are two numbers per feeder, and a feeder contributes sign x (factor x sum-of-its-cells + constant). That is enough for every printed formula on pages 1-3 that is not a conditional, and it is deliberately not enough to invent arithmetic here: this file can still only say which printed cells feed a line and by how much.

`floor` IS THE FORM'S OWN PRINTED INSTRUCTION, not a tolerance. Eleven lines declare it — 1, 6b, 7, 11, Box B, Box C, Box D, Box E, Box F, Box G and Box H — and the page prints a floor over every one of them, in four wordings. (1) on page 2 sits under 'Round to the nearest dollar. Do not enter a negative number. If any line item is a negative number, enter "0".'; (6b) on page 3 carries the instruction inside its own caption, '(If line (6a) minus $3,450 is a negative number, enter "0")'; (11) on page 5 prints the shortest form of all, 'If less than zero enter zero.'; (7), Box B, Box C, Box D, Box E and Box F all sit under 'Do not enter a negative number. If any line item is a negative, enter "0" on that line.'; and Box G and Box H on page 7 each end their own instruction paragraph with a fifth wording, 'Do not enter a number less than $0.' THE OLD REASON HERE WAS WRONG AND IT IS WORTH SAYING WHY. It read 'only a line that subtracts a printed constant can go negative, so exactly two lines declare it' — true of the two lines that existed when it was written, and false as a rule: seven of the first nine subtract no constant and declare a floor because the PAGE PRINTS ONE OVER THEM. A floor is declared from the printed instruction, never from the shape of the arithmetic. When the floor actually fires the gate prints 'floored at 0.00' on that line, so a match that depended on it can never read as an unconditional match. BOX F IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO FIRE ON A REAL RECORD: a household spending more than it earns has a genuinely negative remainder and the form instructs it to print zero. SIX OF THE ELEVEN ARE NOW EXERCISED AND THREE OF THEM CANNOT BE. samples/433aoi.negative.sample.json drives (1), (6b), (7), (11), Box C and Box F below zero and the gate prints 'floored at 0.00' on each. Box B, Box D and Box E cannot be driven negative by any record that obeys the printed instructions: every printed operand feeding them is a non-negative input cell or a line that is itself floored. Box G and Box H are Box F times a printed multiplier, and Box F is floored at 0, so they too take a non-negative operand — their floors restate Box F's rather than adding a reachable one, and they are declared because the page prints them, not because the arithmetic could reach them.

ROUNDING IS NOW MODELLED, PER PRINTED BLOCK, AND THIS NOTE RECORDS WHAT REPLACED THE OLD LIMIT. It used to read "ROUNDING IS NOT MODELLED, AND THAT IS A KNOWN LIMIT — comparison here is exact to the cent". It no longer is. `rounding.blocks` in 433aoi.map.json declares, per printed block, which sentence rounds it and where that sentence is drawn; adapters/pdf/rounding.mjs applies it at OUTPUT and this step applies it at COMPARISON, using the mode of the block THE TOTAL CELL ITSELF sits in. Round first, then floor — the order page 2 y 668.1 prints the two sentences in. STILL NO TOLERANCE ANYWHERE: both sides are brought to the same precision by a printed instruction, and a cell that cannot be is declared not checkable instead. The old note's own example is the case this catches — a market value that is not a multiple of 5 makes X .8 land on a fraction of a dollar, and the page prints the rounded figure while an unrounded recomputation would report a false failure of up to 50 cents per operand.

PER-ROW ENTRIES ARE NOT GROUP TOTALS. Nineteen entries below address a single printed ROW via `total_cell` with a row index, because their printed caption states a formula across the cells of that one row — 'Current market value X .8 = [cell] - [cell] = (3a)'. A group total sums a column; these do not. Both shapes are in this file and they are told apart by `total_cell` versus `total_key`.

(2c) IS DECLARED CHECKABLE ON THE ARGUABLE READING. The map records it as a one-operand equation — the page draws an '=' between the dollar-equivalent cell and the (2c) marker and draws no other operator — with the case against stated: a lone '=' could be decoration on a row the taxpayer carries across by hand, in which case (2c) is plain input. Included here because the arithmetic is identical under both readings, so this entry cannot be the thing that makes a wrong answer look right. Still reported as arguable rather than resolved.

WHAT THE ATTACHMENT CELLS DO AND DO NOT PROVE. (1c), (2d), (3b), (4b-source) and (4b-loans) are declared not_checkable below: what they sum is on an attachment this engine never sees. They are nevertheless OPERANDS of (1), (2), (3), (4) and (4b), which ARE checkable — the page prints those cells, and a recomputation reads what the page prints. The rule is about where a formula's operands are PRINTED, not where their figures came from.

NINE QUICK-SALE TRIPWIRES NOW, ACROSS FOUR PAGES: (3a) on page 2, (5a), (5b), (6a) and (6c) on page 3, (7a) and (7b) on page 4, and (9a) and (9b) on page 5. Every one of them is the same printed shape - a cell whose only identifying text is the ‘X .8 = $’ drawn immediately to its left, with nothing printed above it - and every one is checked against the market-value cell beside it rather than against any leaf name. Eight of the nine leaf names happen to say times_8 or Times_8; the ninth says Times_7 and carries the same printed X .8. That is why none of the nine is bound or checked by name. THE COUNT IN THIS NOTE IS NOW DERIVED: it said FIVE ACROSS TWO PAGES for two slices after the sixth, seventh, eighth and ninth had been authored, while adapters/pdf/maps/433aoi.name-lies.json said nine across four pages about the same cells. Two files in this repo describing one set of nine cells and disagreeing about how many there were is the whole argument for adapters/pdf/count-sweep.mjs, which now derives both from the same place.

THE VEHICLE QUICK-SALE CELLS ARE UNCONDITIONAL AND THE VEHICLE TOTALS ARE NOT. The ‘if the vehicle is leased, enter 0 as the total value’ instruction is printed against ‘Total value of vehicle’, which is the (6a)/(6c) cell, NOT against the X .8 cell. So both vehicle quick-sale entries below are checked on every row whatever the lease answer, while (6a)/(6c) itself is declared not checkable.

(6e) IS NOT AN ALLOWANCE, WHATEVER ITS LEAF NAME SAYS. Enter_Allowance[0] is printed line (6e), ‘Total value of vehicles listed from attachment’ - attachment-sourced input, declared not checkable. The allowance on page 3 is the $3,450 printed at (6b) and (6d), which is a constant the form draws itself and therefore checkable at (6b).

TWO PRINTED CONDITIONALS ARE DECLINED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED, and they are declined for different reasons. (6a)/(6c) branches on the row's own Lease/Own box, which IS printed here - one declarative predicate would recover it, and that is reported to Principal rather than built, because the schema change authorised for this slice was a factor and a constant. (6d) branches on whether the offer is joint, which is NOT recorded anywhere on this form's eight pages - no predicate over a printed cell could recover it, now or later. Recording the difference matters: the first is a gap that can close and the second never can.

THE MIXED-SCOPE FINDING, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT IS AN ARITHMETIC FACT ABOUT BOX A. Box A is drawn under "Round to the nearest whole dollar" at page 4 y 567.5 and adds lines (1) through (7). THREE of its seven operands are drawn under no rounding instruction at all: (5) and (6) are on page 3, which prints none anywhere, and (7) is on page 4 ABOVE the y 567.5 sentence — the sentence is drawn between (7) and Box A. Every operand is nevertheless a PRINTED cell that this step reads back, so the recomputation of Box A sums exactly what the page shows and the tripwire is sound whatever precision those cells carry. What the mixed scope changes is the maximum divergence between Box A and the sum of its operands ROUNDED: see 433aoi.map.json rounding._the_mixed_scope_finding.

SLICE 6 ADDS FIVE ENTRIES AND ONE OF THEM READS ITS OPERANDS OFF DRAWN SYMBOLS. (30) and (31) carry no printed sentence naming their operands: the page draws '$ [ ] + $ [ ] + $ [ ] + $ [ ] =' and that IS the formula. Every other total on this form so far names its operands in words ('Add lines (8a) through (8d) ='). Both readings are printed and both are exact; the symbol one is recorded here because a later author scanning captions for the word 'Add' would find nothing and conclude these two totals are plain input.

SLICE 6 - BOX F IS THE FIRST CELL ON THIS FORM FED ENTIRELY BY OTHER BOXES, and its floor is the first that a real record is likely to fire. Box A, Box B, Box D and Box E all add lines. Box C subtracts one line from another. Box F subtracts one BOX from another, and the printed order of the words is the reverse of the arithmetic - the same trap Box C sets one page earlier.

It is the allowed deduction for professional books and tools of trade, it is capped, and it applies to individuals and sole-proprietors only. Entering more than the published allowance overstates the deduction and understates the offer; entering nothing when it applies does the reverse.

Page 3's vehicle rows print the same shape and there the branch IS recoverable, because each row prints its own Lease/Own checkbox pair and slice 3 declared a feeder predicate over it. PAGE 5 PRINTS NO LEASE INDICATOR: the only four checkboxes on the page are CB5_01..CB5_04, the Notes Receivable and Accounts Receivable Yes/No pairs. If the asset is LEASED, or is USED IN THE PRODUCTION OF INCOME, the printed instruction says enter 0 as the total value — even though the quick-sale cell beside it holds a real figure and the subtraction would produce one. Both conditions zero the row. A preparer who enters (market value X .8) minus loan on a leased machine, or on equipment used to produce income, overstates Box B and therefore the offer, and nothing on this page can catch it.

entries.printed_caption: Net business income from Box C [Deductions for non-cash expenses on Schedule C (e.g., depreciation, depletion, etc.) are not permitted as an expense for offer purposes and must be added back in to the net income figure]
entries.why_not_checkable: THE CAPTION NAMES A PRINTED CELL AND THEN INSTRUCTS THE PREPARER TO MAKE IT DIFFER. 'from Box C' reads as an equality and Box C is printed on page 5 of this same form, so a one-operand tripwire would be exact and would need no new schema. The bracketed sentence beside it is why one is not declared: a Schedule-C net income that included depreciation or depletion must have those added back HERE, so (36) legitimately exceeds Box C by the amount of the non-cash deductions. A tripwire would pass on every form where the add-back is zero and fail exactly the forms that did the harder thing correctly. See _arguable_page6 P6-2. It is nevertheless an operand of Box D, which IS checkable.
entries.review_page_advisory: ADD BACK NON-CASH DEDUCTIONS BEFORE ENTERING THIS FIGURE. Box C on page 5 is the starting point, not the answer. If the business net income was computed from a Schedule C that deducted depreciation, depletion or any other non-cash expense, those amounts are NOT allowed for offer purposes and must be added back in. Entering Box C unchanged when an add-back applies understates household income, understates Box F, and understates the offer.

entries.printed_caption: Enter the amount from either Box G or Box H
entries.why_not_checkable: THE PAGE DOES NOT SAY WHICH. Box G is Box F x 12 and applies when the offer is paid in 5 or fewer payments within 5 months or less; Box H is Box F x 24 and applies when it is paid in 6 to 24 months. Which of the two governs is the PAYMENT TERM, and 433-A(OIC) prints no cell anywhere that records it - the term is chosen on Form 656, Section 4, which this form names three times and which this repo does not hold. So the cell equals one of two printed figures and nothing printed on this page decides which, and a tripwire that accepted either would pass on a form where the wrong one was copied. Declared not checkable rather than checked against a disjunction.
entries.review_page_advisory: This cell must equal Box G (y 633.6, the x 12 row) if the offer will be paid in 5 or fewer payments within 5 months or less, or Box H (y 579.6, the x 24 row) if it will be paid in 6 to 24 months. The form gives no cell for the payment term, so nothing here can check which one you copied - it is set on Form 656, Section 4, Payment Terms. Check it against the term you are actually offering before filing.
